links.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM answers across two independent phases
links.effect: Identical answers across phases in 81.7% (ChatGPT), 81.1% (DeepSeek), 76.1% (Perplexity) of items; reproducibly correct only 52.1%, 48.8%, 43.2%.
links.quote: Identical answers across phases occurred in 81.7% of items for ChatGPT, 81.1% for DeepSeek, and 76.1% for Perplexity, but reproducibly correct answers were 52.1%, 48.8%, and 43.2%.

links.outcome: LLM accuracy on acid-base management and drug treatment MCQs
links.effect: Overall accuracy was 59.8% (305/510) ChatGPT, 58.8% (300/510) DeepSeek, 53.7% (274/510) Perplexity; only moderate performance.
links.quote: Overall accuracy was 59.8% (305/510) for ChatGPT, 58.8% (300/510) for DeepSeek, and 53.7% (274/510) for Perplexity (Cochran's Q p = 0.16); ChatGPT and DeepSeek each outperformed Perplexity (p = 0.0086 and p = 0.0374).

links.outcome: LLM clinical knowledge accuracy on acid-base management and drug treatment questions
links.effect: Accuracy was lowest for metabolic acidosis subtypes (52.5%, 42.4%, 32.2%) and highest for compensation (70.7%, 70.7%, 62.1%); overall about 54-60%.
links.quote: Accuracy was highest for compensation/expected response (116 items; 70.7% for ChatGPT and DeepSeek, 62.1% for Perplexity) and lowest for metabolic acidosis subtypes (59 items; 52.5%, 42.4%, 32.2%).

screen.reason: Evaluates the accuracy and consistency of three commercial LLMs (ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Perplexity) on multiple-choice questions derived from textbook acid-base disorder cases without evaluating a deployment safeguard or practice.
